# Learning inquiry cards: source-verified content proposal

Content proposal verified against installed compact source metadata; not a deployed public-learning workflow.

**How has corn production changed across U.S. states?**

Choose two states. What pattern do you expect to see in their corn-production histories, and why?

- Inspect the same SURVEY measure and native bushel unit in Virginia, Iowa and one other state.
- Change from a recent source-year map to each state’s available time series.
- Which changes might reflect harvested area, yield, reporting methods or weather? Which additional measures would distinguish these explanations?

Limit: USDA survey estimates remain estimates; current-year annual observations may be preliminary or forecasts. A longer state history is not proof of unchanged methods, and production is not household food availability.

- [Virginia corn history](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=nass-food%3A%3Acrops%3Astates%3A846b0bd3f58ffa00&year=2025&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)
- [Iowa corn history](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=nass-food%3A%3Acrops%3Astates%3A846b0bd3f58ffa00&year=2025&place=IA&wb_state=s1_)

**Do nearby counties show the same agricultural changes?**

Before inspecting the records, how similar do you expect two counties’ production histories to be?

- Compare Accomack County, Virginia with Polk County, Iowa, then choose a nearby county for a second comparison.
- Inspect production and yield as separate measures; look for actual reporting years and unavailable cells.
- Describe a contrast that remains when the same commodity, source program and unit are held fixed.

Limit: County coverage varies by product/year; Census and survey series must remain separate. The map uses 2025 outlines, not reconstructed historical borders. Suppression is not zero.

- [Accomack corn production](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=nass-food%3A%3Acrops%3Acounties%3A2ee0b4391e7a2c86&year=2025&place=51001&wb_state=s1_)
- [Polk County corn production](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=nass-food%3A%3Acrops%3Acounties%3A2ee0b4391e7a2c86&year=2025&place=19153&wb_state=s1_)
- [Accomack corn yield](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=nass-food%3A%3Acrops%3Acounties%3A3cc956a1d4db2ca1&year=2025&place=51001&wb_state=s1_)

**How does producing food differ from having food available for people?**

For one country, what relationship do you expect between wheat production and the wheat recorded as available for food?

- Inspect wheat production, imports, animal feed and food-availability quantities from the same food-balance methodology.
- Choose another country and compare actual shared source years.
- Look separately at the longer wheat-production history; check tonnes versus thousand tonnes before comparing values.

Limit: Food availability is a supply-account measure, not measured individual intake or equal household access. QCL and food-balance series differ in scope/units. No older food-balance methodology has been spliced into the 2010–2023 series.

- [Wheat available for food](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=food-history-fbs%3A%3A2511-5142-1000-t&year=2023&place=USA&wb_state=s1_)
- [Wheat balance production](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=food-history-fbs%3A%3A2511-5511-1000-t&year=2023&place=USA&wb_state=s1_)

**How has the energy mix changed across states?**

Which changes in solar and coal production would you expect in Virginia and another state over the retained years?

- Inspect solar energy and coal energy production in their common Billion Btu unit.
- Compare levels and changes over the same years.
- What would change if you compared total output, per-person output, or electricity generation rather than all energy production?

Limit: Energy-content production, electricity generation, capacity and energy consumption are different measures. These source trends alone do not identify policy effects or total life-cycle emissions.

**Where does income appear to stretch further?**

Which two states would you expect to differ in income and prices, and what makes you expect that?

- Compare published household income, real personal income per person and regional price parity as different concepts.
- Inspect rent burden as its own published measure rather than a ratio of two medians.
- Which household circumstances or local distributions are missing from these state summaries?

Limit: ACS household medians, BEA per-person averages and RPP price levels have different populations and adjustments. An RPP is not local inflation or a particular family’s budget; no automatic extra cost-of-living adjustment is made.

- [Household income by state](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=income%3A%3Amedian-household-income&year=2024&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)
- [Virginia regional price levels](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=bea%3A%3ASARPP-1&year=2024&place=VA&wb_state=s1_eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjoxLCJrZXkiOiJsaWJyYXJ5Iiwic2VjdGlvbiI6ImxpYnJhcnkiLCJzZXR0aW5ncyI6eyJ4X3NlcmllcyI6ImJlYTo6U0FSUFAtMSIsImNoYXJ0X3R5cGUiOiJ0aW1lIiwibW9kZSI6InRpbWVfc2VyaWVzIiwidGFiIjoiZXhwbG9yZSIsInZpZXdfeWVhciI6MjAyNCwidmlld19wbGFjZSI6IlZBIiwiZ2VvX2lkIjoiVkEiLCJ5ZWFyIjoyMDI0fX0)
- [Published rent burden](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=cost-of-living%3A%3Amedian-gross-rent-income-percent&year=2024&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)

**How do federal revenue and spending balances differ across states?**

What pattern do you expect for Virginia’s attributed federal balance compared with another state?

- Inspect net balance and per-resident balance from the same fiscal-year vintage.
- Compare several actual years and note preliminary/revised status.
- What roles might program mix, age, federal employment or attribution rules play?

Limit: Attributed federal spending minus revenue is not the state-government budget, a household tax bill or the benefits received by every resident. State tax receipts remain a separate fiscal layer; nominal balances are not inflation-adjusted.

- [Virginia federal balance history](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=fiscal-history%3A%3Afederal-net-per-capita&year=2023&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)
- [Separate state tax-collection layer](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=state-government-tax-receipts%3A%3Astate-tax-total-2025&year=2025&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)

**What can a pension fund’s return tell us about retirement security?**

Before inspecting the definitions, what relationship would you expect between a fund’s investment return and a retiree’s buying power?

- Compare the same return horizon for Virginia Retirement System and Arizona State Retirement System.
- Read fee-basis, estimated-value and fiscal-period notes before comparing.
- List the separate benefit, COLA, contributions and expense information needed to assess buying power.

Limit: Named plan returns are not state averages and are not pension-benefit increases. Overlapping annualized horizons induce dependence; source-review outliers remain inspectable but are model-ineligible. Benefit rules and household expenses require separate evidence.

- [Virginia Retirement System · 10-year horizon](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=ppd%3A%3Areturn-10yr&year=2025&place=115&wb_state=s1_eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjoxLCJrZXkiOiJsaWJyYXJ5Iiwic2VjdGlvbiI6ImxpYnJhcnkiLCJzZXR0aW5ncyI6eyJ4X3NlcmllcyI6InBwZDo6cmV0dXJuLTEweXIiLCJjaGFydF90eXBlIjoidGltZSIsIm1vZGUiOiJ0aW1lX3NlcmllcyIsInRhYiI6ImV4cGxvcmUiLCJ2aWV3X3llYXIiOjIwMjUsInZpZXdfcGxhY2UiOiIxMTUiLCJnZW9faWQiOiIxMTUiLCJ5ZWFyIjoyMDI1fX0)
- [Arizona State Retirement System · 10-year horizon](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=ppd%3A%3Areturn-10yr&year=2025&place=6&wb_state=s1_eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjoxLCJrZXkiOiJsaWJyYXJ5Iiwic2VjdGlvbiI6ImxpYnJhcnkiLCJzZXR0aW5ncyI6eyJ4X3NlcmllcyI6InBwZDo6cmV0dXJuLTEweXIiLCJjaGFydF90eXBlIjoidGltZSIsIm1vZGUiOiJ0aW1lX3NlcmllcyIsInRhYiI6ImV4cGxvcmUiLCJ2aWV3X3llYXIiOjIwMjUsInZpZXdfcGxhY2UiOiI2IiwiZ2VvX2lkIjoiNiIsInllYXIiOjIwMjV9fQ)

**How does the turnout denominator change the story?**

Would you expect a state’s voting rate to look the same when measured among registered voters, citizen adults and all adults?

- Inspect administrative turnout among active registrations and CPS reported turnout among citizen adults.
- Compare education attainment only after checking its adult-25+ population definition.
- What information would be needed before connecting these state patterns to individual behavior?

Limit: Administrative counts and survey reports have different populations and uncertainty. Education covers adults25+, not the same universe as registered or citizen-adult turnout. State associations do not establish how an individual voted or a causal education effect.

- [Administrative registration-based turnout](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=voting-administration%3A%3Aeac-turnout-of-active-registered&year=2024&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)
- [Reported turnout among citizen adults](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=reported-voting%3A%3Acps-reported-voted-citizens&year=2024&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)
- [Education attainment · adults25+](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=education%3A%3Aeducation-bachelors-or-higher&year=2024&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)

**Do these wellbeing measures describe the same experience?**

How similar do you expect maps of life satisfaction, reported depression diagnosis and prescription fills to be?

- Read each source’s population, reporting period and measurement definition.
- Inspect life satisfaction, diagnosis prevalence and selected Medicare Part D prescription-fill share separately.
- Suggest explanations for differences that do not assume one measure is a direct substitute for another.

Limit: Prescription fills cannot diagnose depression; Medicare Part D is not the whole population, and the selected six-SSRI share is not all antidepressant use. Survey, modeled and pooled estimates retain their own dates and uncertainty.

- [Life satisfaction](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=wellbeing%3A%3Alife-satisfaction&year=2024&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)
- [Reported depression diagnosis](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=wellbeing%3A%3Adepression-diagnosis&year=2024&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)
- [Selected Medicare Part D SSRI-fill share](http://127.0.0.1:8772/?series=wellbeing%3A%3Aselected-ssri-fills&year=2024&place=VA&wb_state=s1_)

**Which parts of a coal journey can the records actually show?**

What stages would you expect to be documented between coal extraction and final use, and where might the records stop?

- Inspect Virginia plant receipts and their reported source facilities and dates.
- Open the separate customs-export map and identify its reporting-country scope.
- Mark verified endpoint connections separately from the stages that remain unlinked.

Limit: Plant receipts, state distribution and customs ledgers do not establish one complete mine-to-port-to-foreign-consumer shipment chain. Ownership and environmental overlays retain independent reporting dates; the selected customs exporter is not a worldwide-complete panel.

- [Virginia plant receipts · 2023](http://127.0.0.1:8772/pipelines.html?collection=coal_receipts&year=2023&focus=VA&direction=inbound)
- [U.S.-reported coal exports · 2024](http://127.0.0.1:8772/pipelines.html?collection=trade_coal&year=2024&focus=all&direction=either&metric=quantity)

**What does it mean to say a company controls a resource?**

What kinds of ownership, operation or parent relationships would you expect the word “control” to include?

- Compare a reported asset operator, reported owner and identified accounting-parent relationship.
- Change among the acquired company relationship snapshots.
- Identify which ownership shares or intermediate organizations are actually reported and which remain unknown.

Limit: GLEIF Level2 describes accounting-consolidating relationships, not a universal beneficial-owner field or complete ownership chain. Current identity labels do not reconstruct older company names/locations. Shared names or addresses do not prove the same legal entity.

- [Assets and reported relationships](http://127.0.0.1:8772/ownership.html)
- [Virginia Electric · 2024 relationship snapshot](http://127.0.0.1:8772/company.html?entity_id=gleif%3Alei%3ACQKUMNNZVDJLRYV2PT43&snapshot=2024-12-31T16%3A00%3A00Z)

**How does the picture change when emissions are assigned to production or final demand?**

For a country you choose, which account do you expect to be larger: production-based or final-demand emissions? Why?

- Compare the paired accounts in the same source year and unit.
- Inspect domestic/foreign origins and the actual country history.
- What distributional or local-exposure questions remain unanswered by national accounts?

Limit: These are OECD emissions accounts and modeled allocations, not measured commodity shipments or local exposure. Gross-trade accounts can include repeated border crossings. National emissions do not establish who in a country benefits or bears the damages; environmental scenario extension remains unavailable.

- [U.S. production/final-demand accounts · 2022](http://127.0.0.1:8772/global.html?country=USA&year=2022&metric=production)

**What can a tariff indicator tell us about trade—and what can it not tell us?**

What relationship, if any, would you expect between a country’s tariff indicator and its merchandise-trade totals?

- Inspect a published tariff average and its product/weighting definition.
- Compare trade histories and dated policy-event references without assuming the same year or legal scope.
- Name at least two other changes that could affect the observed trade values.

Limit: A country tariff average is not the legal rate on a specific shipment, and nominal trade totals include price/exchange-rate effects. The retained U.S.2019 disagreement is flagged and omitted from comparative plots; observing policy and trade together is not a causal estimate.

- [Canada tariff context · 2020](http://127.0.0.1:8772/global.html?view=policy&policy_country=CAN&policy_year=2020&policy_metric=applied_weighted_all)

**Which economic conclusions depend on the assumptions we choose?**

If final demand changed for one producer’s output, what other outcomes would you expect to change, and what assumptions would that expectation require?

- Inspect the baseline monetary accounts and the defined input–output equation before setting a scenario.
- Identify what fixed input shares permit the model to calculate and which responses it does not model.
- Propose a competing explanation, a held-out observation and a result that would weaken your preferred explanation.

Limit: The implemented input–output demand calculation is a conditional accounting model, not a forecast of prices, substitution, capacity, employment or household welfare. A scenario must be explicitly calculated; observed patterns cannot by themselves rank broad economic ideologies.

- [Economic accounts and explicit demand scenarios](http://127.0.0.1:8772/pipelines.html?view=economics)
